- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overreaction.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model often lags; forecast should adjust earlier than true price.
- Mean reversion is common in 30-day horizon if model is trending too far from recent 10-day average; pull forecast toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or weak.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope slightly beyond trend.
- If sentiment is low and price is falling, model often undercorrects; allow for steeper downward adjustment to match sentiment.
- Avoid linear extrapolation in volatile periods; use sentiment-weighted smoothing or adaptive decay for short-term corrections.
